items.title: Live: Activist group claims credit for banner stunt at Pauline Hanson's Press Club address
items.description: GetUp! says it is was responsible for the banner that unfurled during Pauline Hanson's first-ever address to the National Press Club. Follow live.

items.title: Pandemic travel credits worth millions about to disappear for thousands of Aussies
items.description: Virgin Australia has been criticised for pocketing $93 million in COVID-era flight credits, which are due to expire within weeks.

items.title: El Niño has arrived and it could be the most volatile yet
items.description: El Niño is declared and scientists say the climate change is making its impacts harder to predict.

items.title: Breaking: 'ISIS bride' accused of owning a slave in Syria refused bail
items.description: A woman accused of slavery offences while supporting the Islamic State group in Syria has had her bail application refused.

items.title: CFMEU accused of 'dark strategy' to generate millions in 'illegitimate' revenue
items.description: An inquiry into alleged union misconduct and criminal links in Queensland hears the CFMEU weaponised workplace agreements to bolster its revenue.

items.title: Trump comes face to face with the targets of his ire at G7
items.description: In France, the US president finds himself among a group of emboldened counterparts, many of whom now seem more comfortable criticising him publicly than ever before.

items.title: Glue Store closes after posting $8.4m loss as economic pain hits retailers
items.description: Glue Store announces its permanent closure, becoming the latest Australian retailer to fail this year.

items.title: Live: ASX up, oil plunges to three-month low while SpaceX becomes fifth-biggest US company
items.description: Oil prices sink to a three-month low on reports the US will allow Iran to start selling oil again, while the Australian share market edges up after a sell-off across Wall Street's tech and AI stocks. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Messi equals World Cup record with hat-trick, as Jordan battles Austria
items.description: Lionel Messi scores three as Argentina beats Algeria, after Erling Haaland scored twice as Norway beat Iraq 4-1 in Boston and Kylian Mbappé's super strike sunk Senegal. Follow live.

items.title: Cambodia says 310,000 suspected scammers left country amid crackdown
items.description: A report by Amnesty International casts doubt on the impact of Cambodia's high-profile scam industry crackdown, finding authorities failed to dismantle the "vast majority" of operations.

items.title: AFL stars' mother recounts visit from Dezi Freeman detectives
items.description: Kay Reid, a regional Victorian businesswoman and the mother of footballers Ben and Sam Reid, confirms police searched her home as part of Taskforce Summit's investigation into the movements of police killer Dezi Freeman.

items.title: Zoo raises chimp on human colostrum after mum accidentally drops newborn
items.description: Rockhampton Zoo is hand-rearing a chimp whose mother dropped it from a height by accident hours after giving birth.

items.title: Two high-profile Star casino executives banned from running companies for years
items.description: Two former executives of The Star Entertainment Group Ltd have been handed penalties for breaching the Corporations Act in connection with a Chinese money-laundering scandal.

items.title: Gina Rinehart's iron ore company flags job losses, reportedly in the hundreds
items.description: Gina Rinehart's Hancock Iron Ore has cut jobs a year after merging its two iron ore businesses into a single entity, but won't say how many.

items.title: What happened when Ann Patchett quit swearing for good
items.description: The bestselling author of books including Bel Canto, Tom Lake and her latest, Whistler, is determined to see the good in everyone.

items.title: Six gaming experts share their favourite video games of the year so far
items.description: From cosy builders to hectic shooters and all the way through to nostalgic adventures, there are lots of gems to enjoy on your favourite game console so far this year.

items.title: Bluey speaks Indigenous language in time for NAIDOC week
items.description: The animated award-winning cartoon series Bluey has been translated into Yolŋu Matha, from north-east Arnhem Land, for NAIDOC Week.

items.title: Two men charged over alleged kidnapping murder of Sydney grandfather
items.description: Robbery and Serious Crime Squad detectives have charged another two men following an investigation into the alleged kidnapping and murder of Chris Baghsarian earlier this year in Sydney's north.

items.title: Sandilands reaches settlement over $100m radio contract termination
items.description: Veteran Sydney broadcaster Kyle Sandilands and ARN Media reach a settlement to end a $100 million contract dispute, which had been playing out in the Federal Court.

items.title: 'Deeply ashamed': Paedophile's handwritten message to victims
items.description: Investigators were knocking on the door of a disgraced Sydney childcare worker within a week of him posting images of children on the darknet after identifying the user through metadata and CCTV.

items.title: What a trillion dollars costs democracy
items.description: Democracy cannot survive trillionaires. We need to start taxing billionaires properly.

items.title: 'No credible plan' for mental health overhaul promised after teenagers death
items.description: Improvements in mental health supports for Western Australian children and adolescents — prompted by the suicide of 13-year-old Kate Savage — risk never being delivered, the state's auditor-general is warning.

items.title: Ngambri people say ACT government has not upheld recognition agreement
items.description: The ACT government has been accused of failing to uphold its agreement with the Ngambri people over the recognition of traditional ownership of the Canberra area.

items.title: Runaway Tasmanian devil Mary recaptured after two-week search
items.description: A spokesperson for Village Roadshow Theme Parks said Mary, the two-year-old marsupial, was found and recaptured overnight.

items.title: Pastoralists take to the skies to track livestock lost in floods
items.description: Closed roads and flooded plains are making livestock inaccessible for some pastoralists, while others are employing some serious technology to track down their animals.
